system.summary: Entick New Spelling Dictionary, London 1781 setting: page–printed-row pairs selecting either unmarked column; headwords, inflections, sound-alikes and fragments, mixed with clear figures and words.
system.notes: Two columns yield alternative words at the same pair. An occurrence table records each selection and every repair. Dictionary placement is not proof that its word yields coherent prose.

prior_solution.where: Justus Sherwood read much of it in 1783: his sketch, enclosed with his 2 March 1783 letter to Mathews, gives most of Nos. 1 and 4, part of No. 3, and only 'an advertisement' for No. 2. The copy also preserves partial interlinear look-ups of uncertain authorship. No later reading found in the sources checked (1888 calendar, Wilbur, Vermont Historical Society collections, Waite, Pemberton's 1972 thesis screened across all 373 pages and his 1976 article, both 1956 Sherwood journal instalments). Fryer's two books (pages not accessible), the intended Hoyt citation (unresolved), Jackson 1958 and Wagner 2026 (inaccessible) are unchecked, so novelty is not proven.

conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling set the research task, 48-hour contribution aim and posting restraint, and ordered the British Library images on 12 Nov 2026. AI agents located sources, transcribed, compared editions, decoded and packaged. No human reading verification recorded.
tools: pre-registered No. 4 page-match test with six shifted-page controls
models: AI agents in earlier 12–13 Nov-labelled research; exact model identifiers not recorded
Codex (GPT-6), packaging and second-reader correction check

solution.what: Sherwood sketch supplied member/new/the/being anchors; found fitting pages/rows in Entick 1781. Adjacent plaintext informed discovery; this was not a ciphertext-only attack.
Frozen No. 4 page-match rule: 8 lemma-page hits, shifted-page controls 1,1,0,3,1,2. Reproduced during packaging. This is a coarse identification test, not a validation of every word.

Compared ten scanned Entick printings; 1781 wins page screen 54/79; row score 96/107 exact or same stem. Gloss score 3/9 misses pre-registered threshold 4 of 5 possible glosses. Identical untested settings cannot be excluded.
Looked up all four messages; retained unverified repairs and kept No. 2/No. 3 decoded, not read. Combined former fifth piece with No. 3 as an explicitly provisional continuation.

Retried doubtful pairs against images and neighbours/digit swaps. Corrected No. 3 216-11 to 218-11, exact Magnanimous L 11; second AI reader confirmed copy numeral and dictionary row. Other middle gaps and No. 4 close remain.

Coordinator AI reader reviewed the full prose/decryption tables of Nos. 1 and 4 with LAC source-page inspection: No. 1 grade B (raw first clause), No. 4 grade A, both read in part. This is not a human review, outside-project independent verification, or fresh validation of every Entick row.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 205 tokens, 159 types, en-modern order 4: reading -2.098 per letter; random keys -2.17 (z 2.3); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -1.875 (mean -1.886, z -22.2); annealer on the real text -1.852. Verdict: underdetermined.

Recorded the 12-13 Nov prior-art results: Pemberton's 1972 thesis (all 373 pages OCR-screened, relevant passages and bibliography read) and his 1976 Vermont History article checked, no reading of these messages and no Entick identification; Mathews to Sherwood 9 Jan 1783 (B.179-2 pp. 162-169) read, no book or rule named; both 1956 Sherwood journal instalments read, neither prints the messages. Fryer's King's Men (1980) and Buckskin Pimpernel (1981) located in catalogues but relevant pages not accessible; intended Hoyt citation unresolved; Wagner 2026 thesis returned 403; Jackson 1958 unseen.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.089; polyphony 0.029; 7 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -1.852

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: Matched a published Entick dictionary setting to the messages using Sherwood partial sketch as a crib, then applied its ambiguous page-row/two-column code. The dictionary was not previously securely identified for this correspondence.

gaps.item: No. 1 repairs and source/logistics clauses; No. 2 415, 153-7, 237-31 and sentence connections
gaps.detail: Dictionary rows and local copies checked; original cipher numerals needed to separate copying slips from encoder errors. BL images ordered 12 Nov 2026.

gaps.item: No. 3 middle: 262-36, 6-26 plus separate sign, 272-8, 90-28, 303-22, 417-9, 224-4, 402-25; continuation 203-19 and plain words
gaps.detail: Both columns, nearby rows and selected digit swaps tried; no connected reading. 218-11 magnanimous resolves the former 216-11 gap. Original leaves ordered.
Still visible as copied; literal and nearby dictionary rows do not recover Sherwood closing sentence. Keep two holes.

gaps.item: Prior art: Fryer 1980 and 1981, the intended Hoyt citation, Jackson 1958, Wagner 2026
gaps.detail: Fryer's two books located in catalogues and libraries, but the relevant pages were not accessible online (lending-only or preview denied); Jackson 1958 unseen; Wagner 2026 thesis PDF returned 403; the intended Hoyt reference is still unresolved. Pemberton thesis (all 373 pages screened) and 1976 article checked: nothing found. Novelty not proven; the print escalation step stays unticked.

gaps.item: Original-hand attribution of glosses and comparison of original figures with the LAC copy
gaps.detail: Original British Library images ordered; copyist hand cannot identify the eighteenth-century glosser. Coordinator AI prose reviews cover Nos. 1 and 4, not a fresh check of every dictionary row.
